answers.explanation: Each processor sticks to its own assigned job.
In SMP, every processor can do every job.
That's the picture: private registers and caches, one shared memory.
Multicore is one chip with several cores; multi-chip is several separate chips.
Both cores share the memory, but each has its own registers and cache.
Both give you multiple processors; they're just packaged differently.
Several complete computers packed into one box.
That's symmetric multiprocessing. Asymmetric assigns each processor a specific task.
